items.title: Essence of Linear Algebra
items.blurb: Animated, geometric intuition for vectors, matrices, determinants and eigenvectors. The fastest way to make the maths behind ML feel visual.

items.title: MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra
items.blurb: The classic full-semester course. Pairs well with 3Blue1Brown: Strang gives you the rigour and the computational fluency.

items.title: Neural Networks (series)
items.blurb: What a neural network is, gradient descent and backprop, then transformers and attention, all drawn out step by step.

items.title: StatQuest: Machine Learning
items.blurb: Bite-sized, very clear explanations of cross-validation, bias/variance, trees, boosting, PCA and more.

items.title: Stanford CS229: Machine Learning (2018)
items.blurb: The mathematical foundations of classic ML: regression, GLMs, SVMs, learning theory, EM and unsupervised learning.

items.title: Applied Machine Learning (2020)
items.blurb: The practical counterpart to CS229: more code, more scikit-learn, and how to actually evaluate and ship models.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning
items.blurb: Bayesian inference, Gaussian processes and probabilistic reasoning, taught with real depth.

items.title: Stanford CS229M: Machine Learning Theory
items.blurb: Generalisation bounds, uniform convergence and modern theory of deep learning, for the mathematically minded.

items.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.blurb: Build micrograd, makemore and finally GPT from scratch in code. The single most recommended hands-on deep learning course.

items.title: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.blurb: A fast, broad survey refreshed every January: sequence models, vision, generative models, RL and the newest frontiers.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders (2022)
items.blurb: Top-down and code-first: you train working models in lesson one, then peel back the layers.

items.title: Stanford CS230: Deep Learning
items.blurb: How to structure deep learning projects, plus careers advice and case studies from industry.

items.title: DeepMind × UCL Deep Learning Lecture Series
items.blurb: Research-level lectures on optimisation, attention, generative models and responsible innovation.

items.title: Stanford CS231n: CNNs for Visual Recognition (2017)
items.by: Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Serena Yeung
items.blurb: The course that taught a generation deep learning for vision: backprop, CNNs, training tricks, detection and segmentation.

items.title: Stanford CS231N: Deep Learning for Computer Vision (new)
items.blurb: The updated edition, with vision transformers, self-supervised learning and generative vision models.

items.title: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models
items.blurb: An hour on what LLMs are, how they are trained, where they are heading and their security problems.

items.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
items.blurb: The full training stack for a general audience: pretraining data, tokenisation, SFT, RLHF and how to think about model 'psychology'.

items.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
items.blurb: Write a character-level transformer step by step, following 'Attention Is All You Need'.

items.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
items.blurb: Byte-pair encoding from scratch, and why so many odd LLM behaviours trace back to tokenisation.

items.title: Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)
items.blurb: Four hours of real pretraining engineering: mixed precision, flash attention, DDP, data loading and evals.

items.title: Stanford CS224N: NLP with Deep Learning (2021)
items.blurb: From word vectors to transformers and pretraining. The standard university route into modern NLP.

items.title: Stanford CS25: Transformers United
items.blurb: A seminar of talks from the people building frontier transformer models, across language, vision and science.

items.title: Stanford CME295: Transformers & Large Language Models
items.blurb: A compact, modern tour of how LLMs are built, tuned, evaluated and put to work.

items.title: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
items.blurb: Build every piece of an LLM yourself: tokeniser, model, GPU kernels, parallelism, scaling laws, data filtering and alignment.

items.title: CMU Advanced NLP
items.blurb: Graduate NLP with strong coverage of prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning and evaluation.

items.title: Hugging Face NLP Course
items.blurb: Short practical videos on tokenizers, Transformers, datasets and fine-tuning with the Hugging Face stack.

items.title: Stanford CS236: Deep Generative Models
items.blurb: The probabilistic foundations of Gen AI: autoregressive models, VAEs, flows, GANs, energy-based, score and diffusion models.

items.title: UCL Course on Reinforcement Learning
items.blurb: Still the cleanest introduction to RL: MDPs, dynamic programming, TD learning, policy gradients, from the lead of AlphaGo.

items.title: Stanford CS234: Reinforcement Learning (2019)
items.blurb: Bandits to policy gradients, with careful attention to exploration and evaluation.

items.title: Berkeley CS285: Deep Reinforcement Learning (2021)
items.blurb: Deep RL in full: imitation, policy gradients, actor-critic, model-based RL and offline RL. The background behind RLHF.

items.title: Stanford CS330: Deep Multi-Task & Meta Learning
items.blurb: How models learn to learn: multi-task learning, transfer and meta-learning.

items.title: Berkeley LLM Agents MOOC
items.blurb: Reasoning, planning, tool use, agent infrastructure and safety, with lectures from people at the frontier labs.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy: Software Is Changing (Again)
items.blurb: Software 3.0: LLMs as a new kind of computer programmed in English, and why we should build for agents.

items.title: Stanford CS221: Artificial Intelligence
items.blurb: Classical AI: search, MDPs, games, constraint satisfaction and logic. The foundations agents still rely on.

paths.title: Math for ML

paths.title: From classic ML to deep learning
paths.desc: Classic ML properly, then neural networks with your own hands.

paths.title: Build an LLM from scratch
paths.desc: From a 1-hour overview to pretraining GPT-2 yourself, then a full university LLM course.

paths.title: Generative AI in depth
paths.desc: The maths of generative models and the transformers that power them.

paths.title: RL & AI agents
paths.desc: From reward and policy to LLM agents that plan and use tools.
